summary: Weekly POC sync focused on quality evaluation and regression checks. Reviewed last week's scoring results — small uptick in hallucination rate on customer prompt set after the last model tweak. Discussed prompt-set curation, scoring thresholds, and guardrail false positives. Agreed on follow-ups: updated scoring spreadsheet, two additional eval runs (quantized + fp32), and security/VPC confirmations. Decided to hold off on expansion to Dedicated until guardrail false positives are below threshold and latency targets are stable.
topics: Deployment mode tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
meeting_header: Date: 2025-12-09 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Location: Zoom | Recording: https://redwood.recordings/2025-12-09-6784
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Patel: alright yeah thanks everyone for joining uh we'll kick off, um this is the weekly poc sync for clearwave quality eval, um quick roll call?
00:08 Alicia Gomez: Alicia here, hi
00:10 Ben Park: Ben on product
00:12 Marta Silva: Marta, security
00:14 Samira Chen: Samira from Redwood SE
00:16 Jordan Patel: cool, ok so agenda — results review, prompt set changes, guardrails, next steps, anything else?
00:28 Alicia Gomez: no that's perfect
00:33 Jordan Patel: ok Samira can you start with the eval summary?
00:36 Samira Chen: yeah sure, so we ran the v2 prompt set against model v1.3 that you had us deploy last week. overall top-1 accuracy was at 86.2% which is basically flat, um but the hallucination metric crept up to 7.9% from 4.3% last run, so that's the item we want to focus on. some of that looks tied to open-ended prompts where the model invents follow-on steps.
01:02 Ben Park: quick q, is that hallucination measured on the strict match or semantic judgement?
01:06 Samira Chen: it's our hybrid scoring — token-match for structured outputs and semantic scorer (bert-sim) for free text plus manual spot-checks. in the spreadsheet i linked we flag anything above 0.5 semantic divergence as potential hallucination.
01:20 Alicia Gomez: hmm ok i remember we tightened a prompt rewrite last week could that cause more inventiveness?
01:25 Samira Chen: yeah potentially, we saw a small drift when we adjusted the instruction to be less constrained — i think the prompt allowed more creative completions. also the KV cache behavior on long context sometimes causes truncation, or we saw 'KV cash' — sorry, i mean KV cache — causing prefix mismatch which makes the model re-generate. transcription: uh the log shows repeated prefix misses at token 120+ which correlates.
01:55 Jordan Patel: can you show a couple of examples?
01:58 Samira Chen: sure, example 12 in the sheet — user asks 'summarize prior meds and recommend next steps' and the model inserted a new med that wasn't in the data. that's a halluc — we put full sample in the doc.
02:14 Tom Reed: is there any chance this is from our data transform? we do trim stop words, maybe we're losing context
02:20 Samira Chen: possible, Tom. we asked for the raw payload and your smaple logs earlier, but could you share the last 50 examples where the halluc occurs?
02:27 Tom Reed: yeah will do
02:29 Marta Silva: on the security side we also want to understand if the model variant you ran had any telemetry sent back, we need assurance for the private env.
02:36 Jordan Patel: good point — all runs in this POC were in Redwood-hosted sandbox with telemetry disabled for customer data. for production private deployments we can enable private control plane and KMS only, but we'll share the security doc again.
02:48 Marta Silva: please send SOC 2 section specifically. and the SAML flow for SSO — we need cert rotation windows too.
02:55 Jordan Patel: noted, we'll attach the security pack to the spreadsheet.
03:00 Ben Park: latency didn't change right? i saw a slight bump in p95 from 320ms to 370ms last week.
03:06 Samira Chen: correct, p50 stable around 120ms, p95 hit 370ms after the batching parameter auto-tuned to larger batches. we can force the per-route batching config down to reduce p95 but that will increase per-token cost.
03:20 Ben Park: okay that's a tradeoff we need to quantify. can you add cost delta estimates to the sheet?
03:24 Jordan Patel: will do — we'll show cost per 1000 tokens for both batching=16 and batching=32 plus quantized run.
03:31 Alicia Gomez: about guardrails — our current whitelist/blacklist is flagging a lot of benign clinical notes as PII. false positives are at like 12% in your guardrail logs.
03:41 Samira Chen: yeah we saw that. those are mostly acronyms that look like PHI. we can tune the regex sets and add a context-based classifier to reduce false positives. the classifier would add ~15ms latency but could cut false pos in half.
03:58 Marta Silva: 15ms is acceptable if it's accurate, but show us the failure modes. we cannot block workflows.
04:06 Samira Chen: agreed — we'll produce a false-positive / false-negative confusion table for a sample set.
04:12 Jordan Patel: on rollback/regression criteria, we proposed thresholds in the deck: hallucination under 5%, false-positive guardrail under 7%, and p95 latency under 350ms for hosted. if any run crosses those we trigger a canary rollback and manual review.
04:30 Ben Park: so with current numbers we'd be flagged on hallucination and p95, correct?
04:33 Samira Chen: yes hallu 7.9, p95 370 — both over.
04:38 Alicia Gomez: do you recommend reverting the instruction change or changing the model?
04:42 Samira Chen: usually we prefer prompt-tuning and guardrail adjustments first because model swaps can be heavier on infra and cost. for example prompt v2 had more permissive phrasing; reverting to v1.8 constrained template brought hallucinations down in a prior run.
04:58 Jordan Patel: Samira, can you run two follow-ups: (1) quantized model run with prompt v1.8 and batching 16, (2) full precision run with prompt v2 but tuned guardrail classifier on. we want to see which axis is most effective.
05:15 Samira Chen: yep we'll run both. might take 24-48 hours for full logs.
05:21 Tom Reed: on infra, if we move to Dedicated later, will we lose the latest kernel optimizations? we've been concerned about patch lag.
05:28 Jordan Patel: Dedicated gets the same runtime, we pass kernel improvements quickly, but there is a small window for certs and maintenance. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput though. private on-prem has more lead time.
05:38 Marta Silva: and the private deployment option supports our HSM/KMS, right?
05:41 Jordan Patel: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys for private. we'll include the deployment matrix in the pack.
05:49 Ben Park: can we also see the A/B breakdown for the prompts — i.e., which prompt variations triggered which class of errors?
05:55 Samira Chen: i've added per-prompt breakdown in the scoring sheet — column F onwards. the short summary is: prompts that allowed "recommend" vs "list only" had higher hallucination. also longer context prompts have more cache misses.
06:14 Alicia Gomez: okay for acceptance gate, i'd like to add an explicit manual review step for all hallucinations above 2% to be conservative — that might slow rollout but it's important for safety.
06:25 Jordan Patel: fair. we can add that to the rollout policy as a canary hold.
06:29 Marta Silva: send the SAML cert rotation details and the SOC2 extract for audit trail retention — we need to review with legal before next week.
06:38 Jordan Patel: got it. we'll attach doc link.
06:41 Ben Park: one more question — are there any known regressions in the recent model family release that map to clinical data?
06:47 Samira Chen: there's an optimizer change in the kernel selection that can surface on long sequences for some archs; we've seen similar behavior on other enterprise POCs but not universally. we'll correlate with your failing samples.
06:58 Jordan Patel: ok wrapping up, quick recap of next steps...
07:03 Jordan Patel: Jordan to share updated scoring spreadsheet; Samira to run quantized + fp32 runs; Marta to confirm VPC/SSO windows; Ben to finalize success criteria; Alicia to share 3 more prompt samples. target check-in next Wednesday same time.
07:22 Alicia Gomez: thanks everyone
07:24 Ben Park: thanks
07:25 Samira Chen: thanks, bye
07:26 Meeting ended
notes: Shared artifacts: eval spreadsheet (https://docs.redwood/evals/clearwave-q1), security pack (https://docs.redwood/security/clearwave-soc2), prompt set v3 (attached in sheet).
final_recap: Decision: proceed with two targeted eval runs before any model or deployment changes; hold expansion to Dedicated until hallucination <5% and guardrail false positives <7%. Next sync scheduled for 2025-12-16.
